newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Bosnian police chief dies in NATO clash - radio.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian police chief dies in NATO clash - radio.

text.p: A hardline Bosnian Serb police chief implicated in ethnic cleansing was killed in a clash with NATO-led peacekeeping troops trying to arrest him on war crimes charges, the independent B-92 radio station said on Thursday.
The report, quoting an international police source, said Simo Drljaca was killed in the northwestern town of Prijedor early on Thursday and that a companion wth him also died.
NATO sources in Sarajevo confirmed a Bosnian government report that an operation to detain war criminals was under way in Bosnian Serb territory but refused to give details.

Drljaca became notorious as Prijedor police chief at the start of the Bosnian war in 1992 when he led Serb paramilitary gangs who drove local Croats and Moslems from their homes at gunpoint under ethnic cleansing.
He was also involved in the setting up of detention camps in the Prijedor area where Moslems were killed and tortured.
NATO demanded his dismissal last year after he and his men threatened peacekeeping troops with banned weapons while the waged a campaign of obstruction against the peace process.
